title: Earth, Universe & Solar System Flashcards
description: Key facts from TNPSC Group II Geography Chapter 1

cards.q: What is the center of the solar system?
Which planet is the smallest and positioned nearest to the sun?
What are the maximum and minimum temperatures on Mercury?
Why is Mercury unable to hold the heat it receives during the daytime?
cards.a: Because of the absence of an atmosphere.

cards.q: Which planet is the second densest planet after Earth?
Which planet is known as the 'Hottest Planet' and what is its maximum temperature?
Why does Venus record the highest degree of temperature in the solar system?
cards.a: Because 98% of its atmosphere is covered by CO2.

cards.q: What are the common names for Venus when seen before dawn and after sunset?
Why is Venus called Earth's twin?
cards.a: Because it is similar to Earth in radius, mass, and density.

cards.q: What percentage of Earth's surface is covered by water and land respectively?
What is the estimated age of the Earth from radioactive dating?
What is the duration of a Sidereal day on Earth?
What is the true period of the Moon's revolution around the Earth (Sidereal month)?
Why does Mars appear reddish?
cards.a: Due to a high amount of iron oxides (ferric oxides) in its soils and rocks.

cards.q: What are the names of the two satellites of Mars?
What is the special feature of Jupiter known as the great 'Redspot'?
cards.a: A tremendous storm on its surface that sends strong bursts of radiowaves.

cards.q: Which is the largest satellite in the solar system?
Why does Jupiter not have any seasons like Earth?
cards.a: It has an almost perpendicular axis with an inclination of only about 2°.

cards.q: How many rings are there around Saturn?
What is the specific gravity of Saturn, and what would happen if a large ocean were available?
cards.a: 0.7; it would float in the ocean.

cards.q: How does Uranus revolve around the sun due to its 98° axis tilt?
Why do Neptune and Pluto appear blue?
cards.a: Because of the presence of methane gas in their atmosphere.

cards.q: How long does it take Neptune to orbit the sun?
What are the first dwarf planets identified?
cards.a: Pluto, Eris, and the asteroid Ceres.

cards.q: What is the main difference between a planet and a star?
cards.a: A star twinkles and a planet will glow without any flicker.

cards.q: Which planets are classified as Solid planets?
Which planets are classified as Gaseous planets?
What is the closest star to Earth after the Sun?
What is the maximum duration of totality for a Lunar Eclipse?
What is the maximum duration of a total Solar Eclipse?
cards.a: Rarely over 7 minutes and never more than 8 minutes.

cards.q: What is the angle of the Moon's orbit to the ecliptic?
Name the asteroids mentioned that have Tamil names.
At what distance does the Moon revolve around the Earth?
According to the source text, what are particles that withstand atmospheric friction and reach Earth's surface called?
cards.a: Meteors (Note: Source text anomaly; scientifically these are meteorites).

cards.q: What is a comet primarily made of?
What is the 'Akash Ganga'?
cards.a: A white streak of light seen on a clear night (Milky Way galaxy).

cards.q: Which planet is the swiftest rotating planet?
Which planet is the slowest rotating planet?
Which planet is the swiftest revolving planet?
Which planet is the slowest revolving planet?
